correctness.rationale: Conditioning on the independent mediator infection and the unanimous warning gives terminal i's marginal p²[1−(1−r_i)p^k]. Summing proves the polynomial and the mean-only dependence of the expectation, not of the distribution. With h=1−r̄, the derivative is k+1+2mp−(k+2)mh p^(k+1). If h=0 it is positive; otherwise it is strictly concave in the interior and initially increasing. Its superlevel set at zero is an interval containing zero. Thus the derivative is positive on [0,1) if the derivative at one is nonnegative, including endpoint equality; if negative at one there is exactly one interior root and strict decrease after it. The endpoint derivative is k+1−m[k−(k+2)r̄]. Perfect warning is the most favorable case for reversal; mk>k+1 implies a minimum of six individuals and exactly the two stated six-person compositions. The perfect-warning maxima are at (1+√3)/3 and the unique [0,1] root of 8p³−4p−3=0 (about 0.94664459815). The source's exact-rational checker was read as text, not executed; the conditioning and derivative argument is a replay for all parameters and does not depend on the finite grid. The scope is the specified two-round family and the expected final count.

value.rationale: A minimal exact witness family separates a final-size reversal from simulation and from changes in peak size or duration. The derivative criterion identifies how warning efficacy and terminal fan-out compete with the directly infected count; at the six-person boundary the reversal even persists for r̄<1/9 and r̄<1/8 in the respective witnesses. The value is the transparent, falsifiable boundary in a controlled model, not a universal six-person claim or a prediction for actual epidemics.
